chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The dawn has already appeared for the man who has eyes.

key_terms.الصُّبْحُ: The dawn, symbolizing the beginning of clarity or divine guidance
key_terms.ذِي عَيْنَيْنِ: The man who has eyes, referring to one with spiritual perception or insight

ai.seo_question: What does the metaphor of dawn and eyes mean in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this concise aphorism from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali employs the metaphor of dawn illuminating the eyes to emphasize that divine truth is inherently clear, requiring only spiritual sight to perceive. This reflects the Shia epistemological principle that guidance is accessible to the *ulul-albab* (those of understanding), contrasting physical vision with inner insight. The statement underscores the immediacy of revelation, suggesting that the light of guidance has already arrived and merely awaits the perceptive heart.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 169. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
For the man who has eyes the dawn has already appeared.
